A cylinder has a height of $h$ and a base radius of $r$. The second cylinder has an identical base but is two times higher. The two cylinders are joined together by gluing one of their bases together. Which of the following gives the surface area of the combined solid?

*Hint: You may use the fact that the surface area $S$ of a cylinder is given by*
$S|= 2 \cdot (base area) + (lateral surface area); = 2 \cdot πr^{2} + 2πrh$
*where $r$ is the base radius and $h$ is its height.*

Two identical cylinders have a height of $10$ centimeters and a base radius of $5$ centimeters. The cylinders are joined together by gluing one of their bases together. Find the surface area, in square centimeters, of the combined solid.

*Hint: You may use the fact that the surface area $S$ of a cylinder is given by*
$S|= 2 \cdot (base area) + (lateral surface area); = 2 \cdot πr^{2} + 2πrh$
*where $r$ is the base radius and $h$ is its height.*

The surface area of the combined solid is
{{field-1}}
$cm^{2}$.

:knowledge-point/title: Finding the Combined Surface Area of Two Cylinders
